transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well. I guess I'm here because... for almost two years now, I just haven't been able to shake this certainty about what's going on at work. 

Ever since a specific commission, I know that a few people in my ensemble started... quietly undermining my work. They do it through little things, like schedule changes, or seating choices. Just... little comments during rehearsals. And they'll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, but... yeah. That's basically why I'm here.
Aside from your beliefs about being undermined, have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?
No. Um... no, nothing like that. I don't hear or see things that aren't there. It's just... what I already told you.

Before this issue at work started about two years ago, would you say you generally trusted people in your life—friends, family, past colleagues—or have you always found it hard to trust others, even before this situation?
Um... yeah. Before all this, things were... normal, I guess. I didn't really have an issue trusting people. It's just... this specific situation at work.

Aside from this situation with your colleagues, how would you say your daily functioning has been—are you still managing your work, relationships, and daily routines as well as you did before, or have things become harder overall?

Um... everything else is fine. Outside of the... the issue with the ensemble, I mean. 

I still meet my deadlines. I'm keeping up with my composing. Uh... I still go for a run most mornings, and... things at home with my wife are basically steady. So... yeah. It's just normal.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that ensemble colleagues are undermining him via schedule changes, seating, comments) persisting for nearly two years. No hallucinations or other first-rank psychotic symptoms are present. Functioning is well-preserved outside the delusional content—he maintains his career, marriage, and daily routines. Premorbid personality was not paranoid or mistrustful; the suspiciousness emerged specifically with a triggering event and remains circumscribed to that theme, arguing against paranoid personality disorder and against schizophrenia (which would require broader psychotic symptoms/functional decline). This pattern is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type.
